topic.title: RAM cartridges and alternate displays in AltirraSDL

ol.li: To create a blank cartridge, choose File > Attach Special Cartridge and an Empty RAM-Cart size, Empty Double RAM-Cart 256KB, or Empty SiDiCar 32KB. To use an existing image, attach/open the cartridge file normally. CART headers identify mapper IDs 94-103; a raw image may require mapper selection.

For RAM-Cart physical controls, open System > Console Switches > RAM-Cart switches. Available switches depend on the attached model. Set the controls required by the cartridge software; RAM-Cart starts with its physical switches clear and write protection active.
Run software designed for that RAM cartridge. Adding the cartridge does not turn its banked storage into ordinary computer RAM.
Use File > Save Cartridge to preserve changed cartridge memory as an image. A snapshot also stores the complete writable image and current latch state.

topic.p: Physical switch defaults persist in the active profile's Hardware category. Reset cartridge latch resets the electronic selection while preserving physical switches and cartridge contents. SiDiCar has four independent 8KB banks; its control arrangement differs from RAM-Cart.

If writes appear ineffective, check the selected RAM-Cart model, physical write protection and the software's expected jumper/module arrangement. Save the image before replacing or detaching it. Snapshots and cartridge image files serve different purposes: loading a snapshot rewinds cartridge contents too.

ol.li: In System > Configure System, select an Atari 400/800 machine and 48K base RAM.
On the Devices page, add Mosaic 64K Select and choose Total RAM. The listed 64K-192K totals include the base 48K; the device supplies selectable 4KB banks.
Use Mosaic-aware software. The selected bank occupies $C000-$CFFF; this is not the XL/XE PORTB expansion scheme.

topic.p: This models the 800-strapped bank-select wiring. The separate 1200-strapped modification, PIA wire and OS-under-RAM behavior are not implemented. Warm reset preserves the bank selection; cold reset clears expansion RAM. Snapshots preserve its banks and selection.

ol.li: Obtain the AF80 firmware and character ROM from your own board or an appropriate source. Each is 4KB; they are different ROMs.
In Firmware Manager, assign AF80 Firmware and AF80 Charset. Adding the display device alone does not supply these ROMs.
Configure an Atari 800 and add Austin Franklin 80 column board through Configure System > Devices. Load software that uses the board.
Select its display in View > Video Outputs, or enable Auto-Switch Video Output. Choose Computer Output to return to the Atari display.

topic.p: The board has its own 80x25 RGBI text output. A normal game drawing directly through ANTIC/GTIA does not become an 80-column program. If output stays blank, check both firmware assignments, machine type, compatible software and selected video output. Atari 800 BASIC requires a left-slot BASIC cartridge; the AF80 firmware occupies the right-cartridge arrangement.

View > Video Outputs also routes registered outputs from devices such as XEP80, Bit 3 and the 1090 display board. Next Output cycles them; Auto-Switch Video Output follows active output. Each device still needs its own compatible firmware and/or driver. For XEP80 driver setup see XEP80 Interface Module; the SDL output menu replaces the older help's XEP80 View terminology.
